title: Latency spike forensics and capacity reprioritization playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
--------

This playbook defines a repeatable, time-boxed process for diagnosing sudden latency spikes in model inference paths and for executing short-term capacity reprioritization actions that preserve customer-visible SLOs while minimizing cost and blast radius. It focuses on production-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated pools, and private gateways) and integrates SLO/error-budget signals with capacity controls and routing fallbacks.

Scope
-----

- Applies to service classes: inference-gateway, request-router, model-worker, kv-cache, and edge-proxy.
- Triggering signal: sustained P95/P99 latency regression that violates SLO or a rapid error-budget burn in a single region/cluster.
- Out-of-scope: planned capacity maintenance, long-term perf regressions requiring code changes (those follow the Performance Engineering workflow).

Key goals
---------

1. Rapidly identify whether latency is caused by load, model-serving regressions, hardware degradation, or dependency cascades.
2. Contain customer impact with low-risk capacity/routing changes and temporary quality-preserving fallbacks.
3. Produce evidence suitable for a post-incident review (timelines, queries, artifact links).

Preconditions & RBAC
--------------------

- Oncall SRE must have access to: Grafana dashboards, Prometheus queries, Kibana/Elasticsearch for logs, internal tracing UI, the routing control plane (traffic-router CLI/API), and the capacity controller (autoscaler and pool-manager).
- Runbook assume two-person handoff for any capacity preemption affecting dedicated tenants.

Detection and initial triage (first 10 minutes)
----------------------------------------------

1. Confirm alert: validate Grafana alert and correlate with Prometheus series. Check:
   - Alert name(s): "inference_p99_latency_alert", "model_worker_error_budget_burn"
   - Time window: last 5m and last 30m
2. Snapshot immediate telemetry:
   - Query P99/P95/P50 for the inference-gateway and model-worker:
     - Prometheus: 
       - model_serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-gateway",quantile!=""} (or histogram summary series)
       - model_worker_inflight_requests_total
       - model_worker_kvcache_hit_ratio
     - Traces: search for span latency > 95th percentile in tracing UI for the timeframe.
3. Determine blast radius: which customers, routes, regions, models are impacted.
   - Use token-level tracing to slice by route and model_name. Example query: 
     - logs: "model_name:\"*\" request_id:*" | json | stats p99(latency_ms) by model_name, route
4. Decide initial response tier:
   - Tier 1 (isolated tenant or non-critical route): use tenant-level throttles and cache warmers.
   - Tier 2 (multiple tenants, significant P99/regression): escalate and consider cross-region routing or model variant fallback.
   - Tier 3 (platform-wide P99 regression / SLA risk): trigger incident and follow Major Incident playbook.

Forensics checklist (10–45 minutes)
-----------------------------------

Collect the following artifacts and attach to the incident timeline:

- Time-bounded traces (5m/30m/2h) for representative requests.
- Prometheus query snapshots (include series names and raw result CSV).
- Representative logs for model-worker pods and the gateway (correlate by request_id).
- Kernel and GPU metrics if model-workers show hardware stress (nvidia-smi, DCGM, dstat).

Essential queries and commands (examples)
----------------------------------------

- Prometheus (example P99 over 10m):
  - avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket[10m])) by (le, route, model_name)), 10m)
- Active inflight by worker: rate(model_worker_inflight_requests_total[2m]) by (worker_pool)
- Cache hit ratio: increase(model_worker_kvcache_hits_total[10m]) / increase(model_worker_kvcache_lookups_total[10m])
- Check pod restarts and OOMs: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=model-worker -o wide; kubectl describe pod <pod>
- Collect GPU utilization and memory errors: ssh to node -> nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv -l

Rapid hypothesis checklist (do in parallel)
------------------------------------------

- Hypothesis A — Load surge: increased requests per second (RPS) with matching increase in inflight requests and queueing.
- Hypothesis B — Model regression: a recent model rollout introduced slower ops or larger KV cache misses.
- Hypothesis C — Hardware degradation: GPU throttling, overheating, or host-level I/O causing stalls.
- Hypothesis D — Downstream dependency: database, embedding service, or external API experiencing latency.

For each hypothesis, capture one quick metric that supports/refutes it within 10 minutes. Attach screenshots/CSV.

Containment and low-risk mitigations (first 15–60 minutes)
--------------------------------------------------------

Use the capacity reprioritization matrix below to select mitigations. Actions are ordered by least-impactful first. Always coordinate with pool-owner if you will preempt dedicated pools.

Capacity reprioritization matrix (decision support)
--------------------------------------------------

Patterns and recommended actions:

- If cause == Load surge and affected == best-effort routes:
  1) Apply route-level rate limit: traffic-router apply-rate-limit --route <route> --rps <value>
  2) Enable burst-absorber policy on gateway for 5–15 minutes (automated knob).
  3) Warm or pin model warm-pool for hot models: pool-manager scale --pool hot-warmers --replicas +2

- If cause == Model regression and fallback available:
  1) Initiate model-variant fallback: router set-model-variant --route <route> --variant <vX-compat> --weight 100 --ttl 900
  2) Ramp down canary traffic: rollout-controller pause-canary --deploy <deploy_id>

- If cause == Hardware degradation on subset of nodes:
  1) Drain affected nodes and shift traffic: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  2) Move critical tenants to healthy pools: pool-manager migrate-tenant --tenant <id> --to-pool healthy-pool

- If cause == Downstream dependency latency:
  1) Increase local caching TTLs for embeddings or configuration where safe.
  2) Rate-limit and shed non-essential background jobs consuming shared dependency.

Immediate mitigation play examples (scripts and templates)
--------------------------------------------------------

- Route throttling template (safe defaults):
  - target window: 60s
  - default emergency rps: 50 for non-critical routes, 200 for enterprise tenant routes (subject to SLA)
  - CLI example: traffic-router apply-rate-limit --route /v1/generate --rps 200 --burst 100 --reason "emergency-latency-mitigation"

- Model fallback example: router set-model-variant --route /chat --variant open-compat-small --weight 100 --notify-team sres@redwood.com

Escalation to capacity preemption (policy and approval)
----------------------------------------------------

- Only trigger preemption when:
  - P99 latency is > SLO threshold for 30m and containment actions above have not restored SLO, OR
  - Error budget burn rate > 10x sustained for 1h in a tenant-critical service.
- Approval path: oncall SRE -> SRE lead -> Pool owner (explicit ack in incident timeline). Store approvals in incident doc.
- Preemption actions: reduce soft-qos for low-priority tenants, evict stateless best-effort pods from crowded nodes, or borrow capacity from a staging pool.

Communication and customer-impact handling
----------------------------------------

- If an enterprise tenant is impacted, notify Customer Success immediately with the incident link and expected timeline. Use the templated message in the incident communication toolkit.
- Public-facing status: update status page only when impact affects multiple customers or base SLA. Leave internal status updates in the incident doc for isolated tenant events.

When to trigger Major Incident and oncall shift
-----------------------------------------------

- Trigger Major Incident if any of the following are true:
  - Platform-wide P99 breach for > 15 minutes across regions.
  - Any customer-facing SLA is at immediate risk (legal/compliance).
  - Capacity preemption would affect > 5 enterprise customers.

Post-incident evidence collection (within 24 hours)
--------------------------------------------------

1. Produce timeline with: detection time, mitigations applied (commands + timestamps), owner for each action, and the final remediation.
2. Export the following to the incident annex: Prometheus snapshots, trace bundles (zip), node-level metrics, and the pool-manager audit log.
3. Classify the incident root cause into one of the following buckets: load, regression, hardware, dependency, or mixed.

Remediation and SRE follow-up (72 hours)
--------------------------------------

- Short-term remediation (owner: oncall team): revert rollout or extend cache TTLs; update canary gating rules to be stricter.
- Medium-term remediation (owner: runtime team): create a perf regression ticket, schedule model profiling run, and add regression test to the eval harness.
- Capacity adjustments (owner: capacity planning): if load surges are recurrent, add headroom or convert some pools to reserved dedicated capacity.

Postmortem & Continuous improvement
----------------------------------

- Postmortem should be completed within 5 business days and include: incident summary, timeline, root cause analysis, contributing factors, impact metrics, action items with owners and dates.
- Run a tabletop within 30 days for incidents classified as Tier 2 or 3.
- Feed relevant findings into:
  - SLO and error-budget reviews for weight/threshold tuning.
  - Model-onboarding checklist for rollout gating.
  - Observability standards for better telemetry coverage.

Appendix: diagnostic queries and useful dashboards
------------------------------------------------

- Key dashboards: inference-p99-overview, model-worker-hot-pods, region-capacity-hedge, kvcache-miss-heatmap.
- Prometheus snippets: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Trace search: span.operation: "infer.request" AND span.duration_ms > 1000

Ownership and contacts
----------------------

- Primary owner: eng-sre oncall (rotation list in PagerDuty)
- Secondary owner: runtime-platform (paging policy in runbook)
- Capacity owner: capacity-planning@redwood.com
- Customer contact: customer-success@redwood.com
